title: Mission: a setting this page can see
drDigitalIntro:
Settings are not decoration. They are how you make a computer suit your eyes, your room and your evening.
• You will change dark mode in your computer's own settings, and this page will notice by itself, because your browser passes that preference on to every website you visit.
• That is worth understanding on its own: some of your settings are visible to the sites you use, which is how they know to show you a dark page.
• The rest of the mission is on your honor — brightness, night light, notifications and storage.
• Nothing here is permanent. Every one of these can be put back in ten seconds.

playgroundTask.goal: You changed a real setting and watched this page notice

steps.say: Change dark mode in your computer's own settings.
steps.detail: Not in this page — in the computer's settings, where it applies to everything. Look under Appearance, Personalization, or Display. The box below changes on its own when you do it.

steps.say: Move the brightness until it is comfortable for the room you are actually in.
steps.detail: Most people run a screen far brighter than they need. The right level is the one where the white parts of the screen match a sheet of paper on the desk.

steps.say: Turn on the evening warm-light setting.
steps.detail: It is called Night Shift or Night Light depending on the computer. It takes the blue out of the screen after dark, which most people find easier on the eyes.

steps.say: Turn off notifications for one app that interrupts you too much.
steps.detail: Notifications are opt-out, not opt-in. Every app assumes it deserves your attention until you say otherwise.

steps.say: Look at what is taking up space on your computer.
steps.detail: There is a storage page in Settings that shows what is using the disk. You do not have to delete anything today — knowing where to look is the skill.

drDigitalSuccess: You changed a setting on your own computer and this page saw it happen. That is not a trick: it is your browser telling websites what you prefer.
drDigitalHint: The first step needs the computer's settings, not the browser's and not this page's. If your computer is already in dark mode, turning it off works just as well.
